# secure-my-app

> Find what a stranger can take from your app. Then close it and prove it closed.
>
> secure-my-app is a Claude Code skill (an Agent Skill) that audits one specific codebase against 65
> named security controls in seven groups, and it is the absence-of-a-control tool rather than the
> flaw-in-a-diff tool: Claude Code's built-in `/security-review` reads a diff and finds the bug in
> code you wrote; secure-my-app reads the whole app and finds the defence you never wrote. Every finding
> carries its proof: the code line, and with a live URL the request and its real output, with secrets
> redacted to a provider prefix plus four characters. Without a live URL most access checks come
> back UNPROVEN. Nothing is fixed until the user approves that specific fix,
> one finding at a time, and no fix is marked closed until the attacker's request is refused AND a
> legitimate user's request still works. It is read-only through phases 0 to 4. It never rotates a
> credential and never rewrites git history on its own initiative. It is not a penetration test and
> not a compliance audit, and it refuses to be described as either. A clean run is never evidence
> that an app is secure. The third gate label is the words "NOTHING CONFIRMED HERE", printed with
> its coverage counts. MIT licensed.

secure-my-app fills a specific gap. Diff-shaped security review cannot see a control that was never
written, and generic security advice cannot tell you whether you needed a control, whether you
already have it, or whether the thing you just added works. secure-my-app answers those three questions
about one codebase, with commands whose output the user can read.

The whole skill rests on one rule: **no proof, no finding; no re-proof, no fix.** A candidate finding
must climb four rungs before it may be reported: EXISTS (file:line), REACH (who can get there),
CONTROL (nothing stops it, through the actual calling role and access path), IMPACT (the asset, named
in the user's own vocabulary). Rung 0 is ABSTAIN and is a first-class outcome: a candidate that stops
short becomes `UNPROVEN`, carrying the reason it could not be settled plus the exact command a human
can run to settle it. Every control check ends in exactly one of `PASS`, `FAIL`, `UNPROVEN` or `N/A`;
an empty grep is never promoted to `PASS`.

Evidence is tiered and every proof line is tagged: `static` (read in the repo), `executed` (run here,
this is the real output), `recipe` (written out for the user, nobody ran it). A tier 3 recipe can
never support a `PASS` and can never close a finding.

Severity is a deterministic lookup on two axes, who can do it, (PUBLIC > ANY_USER > SAME_TENANT >
ADMIN_ONLY) and what they get (ALL_DATA > OTHER_USERS > SELF_ESCALATION > INFO), with two overrides:
a live unrotated credential is always CRITICAL, and anything below rung 4 gets no severity at all.
There is deliberately no score out of 100. What ships is a count and a three-state gate computed by
rule (`DO NOT LAUNCH` >= 1 critical; `LAUNCH WITH KNOWN GAPS` 0 critical and >= 1 high; `NOTHING
CONFIRMED HERE` 0 critical and 0 high), always printed with its coverage on the same line, e.g.
`VERDICT: NOTHING CONFIRMED HERE   coverage 41 checked / 9 unproven / 15 n/a   [static only, no live
probes]`. The rating is deterministic; the scan is not, because discovery and classification are
judgements. `.secure-my-app/surface.json` exists so a second run can be diffed against the first.

Every fix is proven twice, in opposite directions: after the fix the attacker's request must FAIL and
the legitimate user's request must STILL SUCCEED. "Fails" means an authorization refusal from the
application with the record present, not a timeout, a 500, or an empty result from a missing fixture.
A fix that fails either half is reverted from its checkpoint commit and marked `FIX FAILED, NEEDS
HUMAN`; fixes are never stacked.

The seven control groups, in the order an attacker tries them: KEYS (8 controls: secrets, key scope,
rotation), DOOR (9: authentication), ROOMS (10: authorization, RLS, IDOR, tenant isolation, mass
assignment), PIPES (13: injection, XSS, CSRF, SSRF, CORS, redirects, webhooks, headers, transport),
VAULT (8: data at rest and data leaving), FLOOR (10: abuse, cost, business logic, AI
features), SUPPLY (7: dependencies, lockfiles, CI). ROOMS is where the expensive breaches live and where
agent-written code is weakest.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/Aboudjem/secure-my-app/blob/main/README.md): What secure-my-app is, who it is for, how to install and use it.
- [SKILL.md](https://github.com/Aboudjem/secure-my-app/blob/main/skills/secure-my-app/SKILL.md): The skill definition, covering the ladder, the three outcomes, the evidence tiers, the six phases, the severity matrix and the gate, the paired test, the dangerous parts, what it refuses to do, and the honest limits.
- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Aboudjem/secure-my-app/blob/main/docs/quickstart.md): A first run in eight numbered steps on a Next.js and Supabase app: install, answer three questions, read the gate, fix one finding, hand over a leaked key.
- [Honest limits](https://github.com/Aboudjem/secure-my-app/blob/main/docs/limits.md): Everything secure-my-app does not promise, opening on the line that a clean run is not evidence the app is secure: why UNPROVEN is not a pass, why the gate is not a verdict, what it cannot see, and why it is not a pentest.
- [The control catalogue](https://github.com/Aboudjem/secure-my-app/blob/main/docs/controls.md): All 65 controls in seven groups as scannable tables, id, control and what an attacker does without it, one row each. The runnable file holds the DETECT and VERIFY commands.
- [Install in your editor](https://github.com/Aboudjem/secure-my-app/blob/main/docs/editors.md): The `npx skills add` one-liner and the `-a` code and install paths for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, Zed, Continue.dev and Kimi Code CLI, plus the manual copy path and what degrades on an agent with no shell, no network or no file write.
- [FAQ](https://github.com/Aboudjem/secure-my-app/blob/main/docs/faq.md): Short answers to the questions people actually ask: is it safe to run, will it break my app, does it send code anywhere (no network call of its own), does it need an API key (no), how it differs from `/security-review`, whether it fixes things automatically (no), what UNPROVEN means, and the rotate-before-scrub order.
- [Security policy](https://github.com/Aboudjem/secure-my-app/blob/main/SECURITY.md): How to report a problem in secure-my-app itself.
- [LICENSE (MIT)](https://github.com/Aboudjem/secure-my-app/blob/main/LICENSE): Permissive MIT license.

## Install

secure-my-app ships as a Claude Code plugin (in the 10x marketplace), through the skills CLI, and as a
drop-in skill directory. It has no dependencies, no server and no account. Optional scanners
(`gitleaks`, `trufflehog`, `semgrep`, `osv-scanner`) are used only if already installed, are never
installed silently, and their absence never turns a check into a `PASS`.

- Vercel skills CLI (recommended), for all your projects: `npx skills add Aboudjem/secure-my-app -g`. Works in more than 70 agents: pick yours in the menu (https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills#supported-agents). In a script, add `-a <agent>`, for example `-a codex`. Only this project: drop `-g`. Page: https://skills.sh/aboudjem/secure-my-app
- Claude Code plugin, the same skill managed by Claude Code's plugin system: `claude plugin marketplace add Aboudjem/10x` then `claude plugin install secure-my-app@10x`.
- Manual / skill-only: `git clone https://github.com/Aboudjem/secure-my-app`, then copy `skills/secure-my-app` into `~/.claude/skills/`. Copy the whole directory: `references/` is loaded by relative path at run time.

Then say "secure my app before I launch", or run `/secure-my-app`. Flags: `--report-only` never offers
to fix; `--group <keys|door|rooms|pipes|vault|floor|supply>` runs one group; `--live <url>` unlocks
the runtime probes, which are off unless the user gives a URL and says yes.

## Skill

- [Skill directory](https://github.com/Aboudjem/secure-my-app/tree/main/skills/secure-my-app): The full skill (`SKILL.md` plus `references/`).
- [The runnable control catalogue](https://github.com/Aboudjem/secure-my-app/blob/main/skills/secure-my-app/references/controls.md): 65 controls with a DETECT and a VERIFY command each, plus the per-command RLS rules and the three-way read test.
- [Per-stack references](https://github.com/Aboudjem/secure-my-app/tree/main/skills/secure-my-app/references/stacks): What each control looks like in a given stack, loaded only when that stack is detected: `supabase-nextjs.md`, `express-postgres.md`, `firebase.md`, `python.md`. A stack file never adds or removes controls.
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/Aboudjem/secure-my-app/blob/main/AGENTS.md): Instructions for AI agents using this repo, including the rules an agent MUST honor.

## Examples

- [Worked report](https://github.com/Aboudjem/secure-my-app/blob/main/examples/sample-report.md): A full illustrative `.secure-my-app/report.md` for a fictional Supabase and Next.js app, showing the gate line with coverage, four findings across three severities in the six-field-plus-STATUS shape, the unproven appendix, and the "not checked, and why" section.
